cells.tense: What the change left behind is here, and you are the one keeping it so.
cells.act: give one thing and take one thing, in balance
cells.ask: Take help you would wave off — a turn, an hour — and give something back at its own size.
cells.core: Something ended and what came out of it is here, steady and worth staying put for. You can walk into a room with no map and move by whatever light is there, then come back and mind what you built. That is how it lasts as long as it does. When something is offered, you take it, and you pass something back at the size it came, so the exchange runs both ways without anyone keeping score. This week, take one offer you would normally wave off, and pass one thing back at its own size. One for one, running even. You will feel where the exchange lands, and which side of it you have been standing on.
cells.sheetLine: You hold what lasted, and the level stays level.
cells.place: the room where you go without a map

cells.tense: What was won is stable, and you are already braced for the next thing to survive.
cells.act: go once toward the thing that draws you and see what it is up close
cells.ask: Go once toward something that pulls you, and look at it at close range before you decide anything.
cells.core: You built something worth holding, and instead of standing in it you run the next break ahead of time — what might get hurt, what might be pulled out from under. When you were moving through uncertainty without forcing clarity, one step was enough; now you want all of them lit at once. That is the tell. So go once toward something that draws you and see it up close rather than from the doorway, where you can still pretend it is a ruin. Let yourself be pulled before you pick. It will be what you feared or what you left, and either way it stops running in your head and becomes a thing you have looked at.
cells.sheetLine: You're guarding the next loss before it arrives.
cells.place: the room where you go without a map

cells.tense: You kept what survived the change, and you are still standing at the door.
cells.act: defend the direction you chose against the next push
cells.ask: When the next nudge away from what you chose comes, refuse it — say this is the way, and hold it.
cells.core: The ending happened and you did not step past it. You can move through uncertainty with only enough light for the next step, and you have read that as a reason to stay at the doorway instead of walking with the light you have. What survived the change is still in your hands, and you are guarding it from the outside. The next time something pushes you off your heading, say no once, with your feet already pointed where you chose. You do not need the whole way visible. Saying it will show you what staying could not: whether you picked this or just stopped here, and what standing your own ground feels like from inside it.
cells.sheetLine: You kept what lived and still stand at the door.
cells.place: the room where you go without a map

cells.tense: You have been holding what the change left standing, and by your own telling you are just nearby.
cells.act: let the structure act instead of announcing it
cells.ask: Catch one decision this week you made without giving it a name, and keep it as work you did.
cells.core: People calm down around you and jumbled things come out in order, and in your version you only happened to be there. Someone held the shape after everything broke, and that someone was not standing near you. In a situation with no clear next step, that steady hand is what lets the way reveal itself — not guessed, not announced. You do not need to start calling yourself its keeper. Just stop saying it is not yours. Let the order stand as something you made, and watch the moment you stop explaining it away: one decision carried through, one calm that held because you were in it. That is yours. No speech required.
cells.sheetLine: That calm came from you, and you're not claiming it.
